title: 1.5.16 Keep Two, Drop Two
description: Five multiple-choice questions on abstraction, the drop test, and why it is relative to the problem. Checked instantly.

questions.question: What does abstraction mean?
options: Making something simpler by using shorter words
Keeping the details relevant to the problem at hand and discarding the rest
Hiding information so other people cannot copy your work
Describing something without using any examples
questions.explanation: Definition 1.5.3. It is leaving something out on purpose, and you should be able to name what you left out.

questions.question: You are deciding whether to keep a detail. What is the test?
options: Does dropping this detail change the action the reader has to take?
Is this detail true?
Is this detail interesting?
Would leaving it out make the description shorter?
questions.explanation: One question settles every case. Being true is not the standard; being load-bearing is.

questions.question: You are describing a bus route to a stranger. Which detail earns its place?
options: The colour of the bus
The name of every street the bus turns down
How many seats the bus has
The stop where they get off
questions.explanation: Without the stop the description is useless. The other three are all true and none of them change what the person does.

questions.question: Can a detail be completely true and still be worth leaving out?
options: No, if it is true it belongs in the description
Yes, but only if the description is running out of room
Yes: truth is not the standard, load-bearing is
No: leaving out true things is what makes a description wrong
questions.explanation: The colour of the bus is a fact. It is also irrelevant to catching it.

questions.question: Now the person you are describing the route to is colour-blind and cannot read the route number from a distance. What does that do to your abstraction?
options: Nothing: the route is the same route
A detail you had dropped may become load-bearing: what you keep depends on the problem, not on the bus
It means you should include every detail from now on, to be safe
It means abstraction does not work for describing directions
questions.explanation: Change the problem and the same fact changes category. Abstraction is relative to the job in front of you.
